title: Monitoring mRNA Translation and Degradation in Human Cell-Free Lysates
author: Schwaller, Karousis
materials:
16.Before you start, clone, sequence, and purify plasmids encoding the reporter of interest. We use pCRII backbone plasmids encoding a RLuc reporter with a 5′ and a 3′UTR and a template-encoded poly(A) sequence.5 To enable co-transcriptional capping a CleanCap-compatible AG initiator after the T7 promoter is necessary. If you opt for enzymatic capping, GGG consensus is preferred for optimal transcription yield. Figure 1 illustrates the features of the plasmid DNA encoding the synthesis of the mRNA reporter.
Note: As an alternative to encoding a poly(A) tail in the DNA template, a separate polyadenylation step can be performed post-transcription using E.coli poly(A) polymerase.
CRITICAL: When choosing between enzymatic capping (e.g., VCE) and co-transcriptional capping (e.g., CleanCap), consider specific features of the reporter mRNA. For example, short CCC motifs can strongly inhibit translation of enzymatically capped RNAs.7
17.Linearize 8 μg plasmid DNA in 200 μL reactions containing the required restriction enzyme sites at the end of the transcript. The point of digestion will signal the end of the transcript during run-off transcription in the next step. As a reference protocol, we set up reactions containing:a.40 ng/μL plasmid.b.1× CutSmart Buffer (NEB).c.HindIII-HF: Incubate 12–16 h at 37°C using 0.3 U/μL.
Note: To enhance the mRNA stability during translation, linearization should occur immediately after the poly(T) sequence. This can be achieved by using a Type II restriction enzyme such as BsmFI.
Note: The transcription template can be prepared by PCR instead of plasmid linearization.

57.Prepare DNA probes specific to the target RNA by PCR following the guidelines:a.Design primers to amplify a region of 200–500 bp, ideally within the open reading frame or 3′UTR of the target RNA. Avoid regions with strong secondary structure or extreme GC content.b.Use 0.04 ng/μL plasmid DNA as template.c.Use 0.3 μM of each gene-specific primer.d.Perform PCR using 1× CloneAmp HiFi Premix (Takara) or an equivalent DNA polymerase, following the manufacturer’s recommended cycling conditions.58.Gel purification of PCR product:a.Add 6× Gel Loading Dye Purple and run the PCR products on a 2% agarose gel with 10 μg/mL ethidium bromide in 1× TAE buffer at 100 V for 20 min.b.Visualize DNA under UV and excise the specific band corresponding to the expected probe size.c.Excise bands and purify DNA using the NucleoSpin Gel and PCR Clean-up Kit (Macherey-Nagel) according to the manufacturer’s protocold.Elute in RNase-free water and quantify using NanoDrop. Store probes at −20°C until use.59.Prepare α-32P-dCTP labeled single-stranded DNA probe using fresh [α-32P]dCTP (half-life: 14.3 days), the purified PCR product from step 9 and the DecaLabel DNA Labeling Kit (Thermo Fisher). We routinely prepare 100 ng of labeled probe per membrane in 50 μL reactions.
Note: Non-radioactive alternatives such as fluorescently labeled probes may also be used for hybridization-based detection, although we have not tested these in this protocol and their efficiency should be validated independently.
60.Purify the labeled probe using MicroSpin G-50 columns (Amersham, Cytiva) following manufacturer’s instructions to remove unincorporated nucleotides. Proceed immediately to hybridization or store short-term at −20°C in a lead-shielded container.

steps.title: Thaw and recover HeLa S3 cells
steps.instruction: Thaw a frozen HeLa S3 vial containing 5 × 10⁶ cells in a 37 °C water bath, transfer to 10 mL pre‑warmed DMEM+/+ (DMEM with FCS and antibiotics), pellet at 200 g for 5 min, discard supernatant, resuspend in 10 mL fresh DMEM+/+, seed into a 75 cm² tissue‑culture flask and incubate at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ until ~80‑90 % confluency.

steps.title: Expand adherent HeLa S3 cells
steps.instruction: Passage the cells twice using trypsinization; after the first passage transfer to a 150 cm² flask to increase yield; monitor viability with Trypan Blue and ensure >90 % viability before moving to suspension culture.

steps.title: Transition cells to suspension culture
steps.instruction: Transfer cells into sterile vented suspension flasks containing DMEM+/+; start with ~20 mL and gradually add DMEM+/+ to keep cell density between 0.15 × 10⁶ and 1.2 × 10⁶ cells/mL; increase culture volume and flask size as needed, never exceeding one‑third of flask volume; incubate at 37 °C, humidified shaker, 80–100 rpm, 5 % CO₂; add fresh DMEM+/+ every other day, diluting 1:4 to maintain optimal density; keep total culture time ≤4 weeks from thaw to avoid drift.

steps.title: Pre‑cool buffers and equipment
steps.instruction: Place PBS and translation buffer (TB) on ice; pre‑cool all centrifuges and the dual‑centrifuge device at 500 rpm for 15 min at –5 °C.

steps.title: Grow cells to target density
steps.instruction: Grow HeLa S3 cells to a concentration of 0.8–1.5 × 10⁶ cells/mL with >90 % viability; typical culture volumes of 250 mL–1 L yield 1–6 mL translation‑competent lysate.

steps.title: Count cells and calculate TB volume
steps.instruction: Remove 2–4 mL of culture, vortex 5 s to reduce clumps, count viable cells; calculate the required volume of translation buffer using 2 × 10⁸ cells per mL of TB.

steps.title: Prepare translation buffer on ice
steps.instruction: Prepare the calculated volume of TB (see Materials) and keep it on ice.

steps.title: Pellet cells
steps.instruction: Centrifuge cells at 500 g for 5 min at 4 °C in 50 mL or 500 mL tubes as appropriate; discard supernatant (use a vacuum pump if the pellet is unstable); keep all buffers and cells on ice and proceed within ≤15 min (max 20 min).

steps.title: Wash I
steps.instruction: Tap tube gently, resuspend pellet in 20 mL ice‑cold PBS, transfer to a 50 mL conical tube, spin at 500 g for 5 min at 4 °C, discard supernatant.

steps.title: Wash II
steps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in 5 mL ice‑cold PBS in the same 50 mL tube, spin at 500 g for 5 min at 4 °C, discard supernatant.

steps.title: Add translation buffer to pellets
steps.instruction: Add the calculated TB volume to the cell pellets, gently resuspend with a 1 mL pipette; combine all pellets into one 50 mL tube. Use ~4/5 of the total TB to resuspend each pellet in its original tube, then rinse the original tubes with the remaining TB and add the rinses to the same 50 mL tube.

steps.title: Distribute suspension into dual‑centrifuge tubes
steps.instruction: Aliquot the homogeneous cell suspension into 2 mL dual‑centrifuge‑compatible tubes, adding 400–800 µL per tube to ensure equal lysis forces.

steps.title: Dual centrifugation lysis
steps.instruction: Perform dual centrifugation for 4 min at 500 rpm, –5 °C (conditions optimized for HeLa S3 cells).

steps.title: Clarify lysate by high‑speed spin
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the lysate at 13 000 g for 10 min at 4 °C; collect and pool the supernatant, inverting the tube gently 4–5 times to mix.

steps.title: Aliquot and store lysate
steps.instruction: Aliquot lysate into 50–200 µL portions, snap‑freeze in liquid nitrogen, and store at –70 °C.

steps.title: Linearize plasmid DNA
steps.instruction: Set up a 200 µL digestion containing 8 µg plasmid DNA (40 ng/µL), 1× CutSmart Buffer (NEB), and HindIII‑HF at 0.3 U/µL; incubate 12–16 h at 37 °C. (If the poly(A) tail is encoded, a Type II enzyme such as BsmFI may be used to cut immediately after the poly(T) sequence.)

steps.title: Verify digestion on agarose gel
steps.instruction: Load 500 ng of the digested DNA and 500 ng of uncut plasmid on a 1 % agarose gel; run the gel to confirm complete digestion.

steps.title: Purify linear DNA
steps.instruction: Purify the linearized DNA using the ChIP DNA Clean & Concentrator Kit (Zymo Research); elute in 10 µL elution buffer and use the entire eluate for in‑vitro transcription.

steps.title: Thaw lysate and keep components on ice
steps.instruction: Thaw lysate aliquots on ice and keep all reaction components on ice.

steps.title: Denature RNA prior to translation
steps.instruction: Heat the in‑vitro transcribed and capped RNA at 65 °C for 5 min. For RNAs with structured 5′UTRs, cool to 20–24 °C over 5 min to allow refolding; for unstructured RNAs, cool immediately on ice.

steps.title: Assemble translation reaction
steps.instruction: In a RNase‑free 1.5 mL tube combine to a final volume of 12.5 µL: HeLa S3 lysate to give 1 × 10⁸ cell equivalents/mL (stock typically 2 × 10⁸ cell eq./mL), reporter RNA to a final concentration of 5 fmol/µL, 1 U/µL murine RNase inhibitor, and nuclease‑free water to volume. For a negative‑control reaction, add 0.1 mM cycloheximide (CHX).

steps.title: Incubate translation reactions
steps.instruction: Incubate the reactions for 50–60 min at 37 °C without agitation; after incubation place all reactions on ice until luminescence measurement.

steps.title: Measure luminescence and analyze data
steps.instruction: Measure Renilla luciferase activity using a plate reader with an integration time of 0.3 s per well. Perform at least three biological and three technical replicates per condition. Normalize raw values to a designated control (e.g., untreated lysate or control mRNA) within the same experiment. Analyze data in Excel or GraphPad Prism; use unpaired two‑tailed Student’s t‑test or one‑way ANOVA as appropriate, with significance set at p < 0.05.

steps.title: Prepare DNA probes for Northern blot
steps.instruction: PCR‑amplify a 200–500 bp region using 0.04 ng/µL plasmid DNA as template, 0.3 µM each gene‑specific primer, and 1× CloneAmp HiFi Premix (Takara) following the manufacturer’s cycling conditions. Add 6× Gel Loading Dye Purple, run the PCR product on a 2 % agarose gel with 10 µg/mL ethidium bromide in 1× TAE at 100 V for 20 min, visualize under UV, excise the band, and purify DNA with the NucleoSpin Gel and PCR Clean‑up Kit (Macherey‑Nagel). Elute in RNase‑free water, quantify with NanoDrop, and store probes at –20 °C until use.

steps.title: Radiolabel DNA probe
steps.instruction: In a 50 µL reaction prepare 100 ng of the purified PCR product, fresh [α‑32P]dCTP (half‑life 14.3 days), and the DecaLabel DNA Labeling Kit (Thermo Fisher) according to the kit protocol. Purify the labeled probe using MicroSpin G‑50 columns (Amersham, Cytiva) to remove unincorporated nucleotides. Use the probe immediately for hybridization or store short‑term at –20 °C in a lead‑shielded container; ensure columns are properly equilibrated and not overloaded.
